Wildlife reserves are dedicated areas for conserving and managing animals and their habitats. They focus on protecting rare, endangered, or specific animals by carefully managing their living spaces to increase their numbers. Similar to national parks, activities like poaching, hunting, tree cutting, grazing domestic animals, and constructing houses are strictly forbidden in wildlife reserves. Entry for people and facilities that could impact wildlife negatively, including tourism-related development, is also restricted. Nepal has one Wildlife Reserve, namely Koshi Tappu, covering a total area of 175 sq. km. This reserve serves as a sanctuary for the protection of wildlife.
i. Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve experiences three seasons.
